text: The mutton dum biryani was packed with rich flavor and tender meat. We waited about 20 minutes for a table on a Saturday evening. Bill came around ₹1,400 for two, which is pretty standard for the area.
The tandoori chicken and garlic naan were absolutely delicious and smoky. But waiting over 45 minutes just to get seated, plus another half hour for the food, completely ruined our evening.

Hands down the best butter chicken in Bengaluru, perfectly balanced gravy and succulent chicken chunks. The captain was very courteous and helped recommend the kulchas. Table took around 15 mins to open up, which is expected for peak hours.
Expected authentic North Indian flavors, but the Lucknowi biryani was overwhelmingly oily and the paneer tikka was rubbery and bland. Really disappointing meal.
Staff here is remarkably attentive and polite. They replaced our water glasses instantly and handled our special dietary requests without any fuss.

The dal makhani and roomali rotis were exceptional, and the waitstaff took wonderful care of us throughout the meal. It is just agonizing having to stand outside in the queue for nearly an hour on a Friday night.
Terrible service attitude from the floor staff. We had to ask four different waiters just to get extra spoons and the bill took ages to arrive because they kept ignoring our hand waves.
That smoky tandoori pomfret and the melt-in-the-mouth galouti kebabs are pure perfection! Absolutely bursting with traditional spice blends.
Seated right away without any delay on a Sunday afternoon, which was a pleasant surprise! The staff was super prompt, clearing plates efficiently and keeping everything seamless.
Easily some of the best North Indian food in town. The paneer lababdar paired with butter naan is out of this world.
The chicken biryani had decent rice and spices, neither exceptional nor bad, just standard restaurant fare. Gravy was okay too.

Waited nearly 50 minutes just for a table only to be served lukewarm, dry chicken kebabs and salty dal. Credit to our server who was very apologetic and polite, but the kitchen took forever and dropped the ball on cooking.
The decor is average with typical warm lighting and basic seating. Hygiene seemed passable, though a few tables nearby could have been wiped down faster.
Awful experience with the food. The biryani smelled stale, the meat was tough, and the tandoori roti was rock hard like cardboard. Couldn't even finish half of it.

The interiors are gorgeous with lovely ethnic brass accents and cozy booths. Food was incredible, especially the murgh malai tikka which was super creamy. Service was regular, nothing noteworthy either good or bad.
Tandoori platter and bhuna gosht were genuinely tasty with great spices. However, charging ₹620 for a modest portion of curry and ₹120 per naan is daylight robbery.

Such a charming, aesthetic place with soft instrumental music creating the perfect vibe. The Awadhi biryani was phenomenal, and paying only around ₹1100 for two people felt like an absolute steal for this quality!
The hospitality here is next level. Our server was smiling, guided us through the menu patiently, and made sure our toddler was comfortable.
The chicken dum biryani has that heavenly aroma of pure ghee and kewra water. Perfection in every single bite!
Loved the warm, heritage-inspired decor and cozy seating. The mutton rogan josh was rich and deeply flavorful, yet the entire bill was under ₹1500 for three of us. Brilliant value!
The atmosphere inside is fantastic—tasteful Mughal-inspired lighting, pleasant background ghazals, and an overall elegant vibe.
Outstanding tandoori spread! The reshmi kebabs melted like butter, and the waiters were remarkably courteous and quick to refill our drinks.
Really enjoyed the Amritsari kulcha and creamy dal tadka, very authentic Punjabi flavors that hit the spot.

The interior decor is classy and elegant with beautiful ambient lighting. Both the mutton biryani and paneer tikka were rich and delicious. We waited roughly 15 minutes for our table, and the final check of ₹1,600 for two seemed standard for dining out here.
The restaurant looks stunning with rustic wooden fixtures and royal decor. But ₹550 for a tiny bowl of paneer gravy and ₹180 for lime soda is ridiculously steep.
The butter chicken paired with hot garlic naan was thoroughly rich and flavourful. Paying just around ₹650 for two people in Koramangala is an absolute steal.
Super impressed with how tidy everything was kept despite the rush. The dining tables were wiped down immediately, cutlery was sparkling clean, and even the handwash area was spotless.
Loved the warm amber lighting and soothing instrumental sitar music playing in the background. The decor gives off such an elegant royal vibe, making it perfect for family dinners.

The Lucknowi dum biryani was cooked to perfection with tender meat falling off the bone. Our server was very courteous and attentive throughout, and the earthy, regal interiors made the whole meal even better.

Really nice lighting and rustic vibe, plus the bill came to barely ₹800 which is super reasonable. Staff just did their routine job without much interaction, but they need to pay attention to hygiene because our table still had oily smudges and crumbs from the previous guests.

The murgh malai tikka literally melts in your mouth and charges are so pocket friendly with starters around ₹260. The staff completely ignored our table when we asked for water refills twice, but honestly the food was so heavenly and cheap that I don't care.

Their dal makhani is rich and packed with authentic Punjabi flavours, no doubts there. Hygiene is about average like any typical busy eatery. But the waiter who took our order seemed thoroughly uninterested and practically threw the bill booklet at us.
Best mutton rogan josh I have eaten in Bangalore! Gravy had phenomenal depth and the meat was succulent.
Tandoori platter was smoky and well seasoned, specially the fish tikka which was super fresh and flaky.
The hospitality here is top tier. Our waiter gave great recommendations and made sure our toddler had extra cushions and warm milk without us even having to chase anyone down.
Had the chicken biryani and butter roti for lunch. Taste was strictly average, nothing bad but not something I would crave again either.
Outstanding saffron dum biryani, each grain of basmati was aromatic and spiced to absolute perfection.

We were seated immediately on a Friday evening and our piping hot tandoori chicken arrived in less than ten minutes. Service was just standard plate-clearing, but the smoky flavour and juicy texture of the meat blew us away.
Those galouti kebabs with ulte tawe ka paratha are pure bliss. melt in mouth perfection!
Had to wait about twenty minutes on a Sunday afternoon to get a table for four. Standard waiting period for a busy joint in this area.

Flawless dining experience! The Sikandari raan was magnificent, we got our table without any wait, and the place smelled fresh with gleaming floors. Beautiful traditional brass decor adds so much charm to the evening.
Staff was exceptionally polite and kept clearing empty plates promptly without being intrusive.

The kadai paneer and roomali roti were genuinely delicious with authentic North Indian spices. Too bad the waitstaff took forty minutes to bring our raita and completely forgot the drinks until we reminded them three times.
Ordered the shahi paneer and jeera rice; it was okay, gravy felt a bit generic and lacked that authentic tandoori punch.

The host and servers were incredibly courteous and apologized multiple times for the chaos. Still, making diners wait almost 50 minutes outside on the pavement despite booking in advance was really frustrating.
Rich, slow-cooked bhuna gosht served with crisp laccha paratha was super satisfying.
Really enjoyed the tandoori malai broccoli and paneer lababdar, very comforting flavours.

The kebabs were meltingly tender and the service team was warm and proactive throughout our dinner in their cozy, dimly lit dining room. My only gripe is the pricing, as nearly ₹3,200 for a modest family dinner feels a bit steep for the portion sizes.
Total value for money! You get hearty North Indian portions for barely ₹250 to ₹300 a dish, which is rare to find around Indiranagar these days.
The Awadhi mutton biryani here is legendary, and finishing with their hot gulab jamun made my weekend.
We stood in the queue outside for almost an hour on a Friday night, and once seated it took another 40 minutes just for starters. Totally killed the appetite.
The Awadhi mutton dum biryani is exceptional! Tender meat, fragrant long-grain basmati, and subtle whole spices that don't overwhelm.
Really enjoyed the tandoori pomfret and paneer tikka, perfectly charred and juicy.
The staff was very attentive throughout our dinner and the dal makhani with garlic naan tasted heavenly. However, ₹520 for a basic curry portion felt quite overpriced for the quantity served.
Hands down the best murgh malai tikka in Indiranagar. The waiter was prompt and polite, and paying barely ₹1,200 for a hearty meal for two is an absolute steal.
Found dirty cutlery on the table and sticky grease all over the menu cards. The handwash sink near the back was filthy and overflowing.
Warm hospitality from the team, right from greeting us at the door. And that Lucknowi chicken biryani paired with burani raita was sheer perfection.

The wait was around 20 minutes before getting a table, which is pretty standard. At just ₹280 per biryani, the bill was very light on the wallet, but the chicken pieces were dry and the rice lacked any real flavour.
Had to wait 45 painful minutes for a table even with an advance booking. Thankfully, our server was genuinely sweet and tried his best to rush our order once we finally sat down.
The servers completely ignored our table after dropping off the water glasses. Had to wave three times just to ask for the bill, and nobody bothered to check if we needed more bread.
Spotless dining hall and sparkling clean plates, which I always look for first. The smoky aroma of their tandoori broccoli and tender seekh kebabs blew us away!
Best butter chicken and butter naan combo in Bengaluru, period.
The mutton rogan josh was overly salty and swimming in a layer of grease. Biryani had zero aroma and felt like it was just reheated in a microwave.
Exceptional dining experience with very cordial staff who recommended the house special kebabs. Everything from the galouti kebabs to the saffron phirni was sublime.

The mutton dum biryani and roomali rotis were genuinely delicious and authentic. The decor is standard North Indian family restaurant style, and ₹1,800 for three people is neither cheap nor exorbitant.
Quick service and courteous waiters who refilled our glasses without asking. The smoked butter chicken hit the spot nicely.
The floor staff were super polite and accommodated our requests effortlessly. Sadly, the dining room was so terribly loud and cramped that we could barely hear each other speak across the table.
Lovely warm lighting and tasteful classical instrumental music made for a very cosy dinner. Kebabs were succulent and flavorful, while the dining area hygiene seemed acceptable and average.
Super clean restrooms and neatly sanitized tables. We loved the heritage aesthetic with royal brass cutlery, and paying under ₹1,000 for dinner in this part of town is unbelievable value!
Charming rooftop vibes with tasteful Sufi music playing in the background. The signature Saffron Table biryani with soft shorba was absolute bliss.
Huge portions of rich mutton nihari and khameeri roti at very pocket-friendly rates. Great taste without burning a hole in your pocket.
The hospitality here is top tier. Our waiter took great care of our elderly parents and made sure every single request was handled promptly.
Impeccably clean floors and tables, giving off a very hygienic vibe. Given how reasonable the bill came out to be, it's easily one of the best value spots in the city.
The staff is remarkably polite, well-groomed, and attentive. The restaurant is maintained in pristine condition with spotless cutlery and clean wash areas.
Flavourful chicken lababdar with piping hot lachha parathas, and the captain was very helpful with suggestions. Just felt ₹480 for a small bowl of curry is pushing the budget a bit too far.
We got seated after around 20 minutes on a Saturday afternoon, which is typical for Koramangala. Had a standard lunch before heading back to work.
Best Lucknowi mutton biryani in Bengaluru! Meat was fork-tender and fragrant with saffron.
The wait was roughly 25 minutes for a table of four on Friday night.
We put our names down and waited about 15 minutes at the entrance. The murgh malai tikka and butter naan were absolute perfection—so buttery and smoky!
Loved the dal makhani and garlic naan, rich and full of flavour. But ₹420 for a small bowl of dal feels way too steep for regular dining.

Lovely warm lighting and tasteful Sufi instrumental music playing in the background. We waited around 20 mins for our table, but once seated, the waiters completely ignored us and forgot our water refill twice.
The tandoori pomfret had a crisp char and great spice coating. Really enjoyed the cozy booth seating and subtle brass decor.
Outstanding hospitality from the staff who recommended the galouti kebabs. They literally melt in your mouth, paired with flaky ulta tawa paratha!
Tandoori chicken here has ruined all other places for me, perfectly juicy right to the bone.
That dum pukht gosht biryani is pure magic. Each grain of basmati rice soaked in aroma.
Paneer lababdar was creamy with just the right hint of sweetness, and the kulchas were nicely crisp.
The bill came out to around ₹1,400 for two people, pretty standard rates for Indiranagar casual dining.
Awful experience. The chicken tikka was dry and rubbery, and the biryani tasted completely bland with undercooked rice grains.

Walked straight in on a Tuesday with zero wait! At just ₹350 for the lunchtime thali, it is incredible value given how mouthwatering the korma and subz biryani were. Decor is the usual North Indian diner setup and the waiter just took our order and brought the bill.
Waited over 55 agonizing minutes outside in the humidity just to get a basic two-seater table. Totally disorganized queue management.
Around a 15-minute wait by the door. The paneer tikka and butter chicken gravy were phenomenal, rich without feeling too greasy.
Easily top-tier mutton seekh kebabs in the city! Spiced to perfection.
Spent about ₹1,800 for two adults and a kid, which is about what you expect for North Indian food here.
The chicken biryani was okay, neither bland nor particularly memorable. Service was standard—they took the order and cleared the plates on time.
Authentic flavours! The bhuna gosht paired with butter naan hit the spot on a rainy Bengaluru evening.
Massive portions for such reasonable prices! We fed four people hearty tandoori platters and biryani for barely ₹1,200 total.
Sensational tangdi kebab and the smoothest dal makhani I've had in ages.
The tables, cutlery, and floors were impeccably clean and spotless. Loved the aromatic mutton biryani, though the server seemed visibly irritated whenever we asked for extra chutney.
The reshmi kebabs are out of this world, so soft and packed with smoky spice!

Stood in the waiting area for about twenty minutes before our token was called. The staff were exceedingly polite, constantly checking if we needed fresh naans and serving everything with a warm smile.
The waiters completely ignored our table on a Friday evening. We had to ask four different times just to get a jug of water and an extra fork.
Hands down the best mutton dum biryani in Bengaluru! The meat was meltingly tender and the spice balance in the salan was sheer perfection.
Really enjoyed the murgh malai tikka and garlic naan, both were fresh and full of flavor. Our server was very attentive and made great recommendations throughout our meal.
Disappointed with the butter chicken; it tasted overwhelmingly sweet like tomato ketchup and the chicken chunks were tough and rubbery.
Tandoori pomfret was charred to smoky perfection with crisp skin and juicy flesh. Will definitely order the tandoor platter again next time.
The dining hall was suffocatingly noisy and deafeningly loud music was blasting right over our heads. It felt more like a chaotic railway platform than a relaxing dinner venue.
The paneer butter masala paired with lachha paratha was rich and delicious. The staff took our order and served the plates as expected without much interaction.
Sublime Lucknowi mutton biryani, fragrant long-grain basmati and zero excess grease. Even the burani raita had a lovely garlic punch.
The dining area and washrooms were spotless and very well maintained. Sadly, the staff was aloof and took forever to hand us the bill after we finished eating.
The dal makhani and tandoori roti were standard fare. Nothing bad about the meal, but nothing particularly memorable either.

The chicken seekh kebabs were juicy and packed with herbs, and the waiter constantly refilled our water glasses with a polite smile. The interior decor is pretty generic for an Indiranagar eatery, neither striking nor bad.
Impressed by the hygiene standards here. The cutlery was gleaming, tables were sanitized immediately after guests left, and hand wash stations were tidy.
Everything from the Awadhi biryani to the gulab jamun was phenomenal! On top of that, the kitchen counter and open serving stations were immaculately clean.
The smoky tangdi kebabs tasted incredible, cooked just right over charcoal. The dining tables and polished floor were exceptionally tidy too.
Our order took about 25 minutes to arrive, which is standard on a busy Sunday night. The bill came out to around ₹1,400 for two people, pretty typical for this neighborhood.
Getting this generous portion of royal chicken biryani and two roomali rotis for under ₹500 is an absolute steal in this area! Outstanding value for money.

Waited 50 agonizing minutes just for starters, and the servers were rude whenever we checked on the status. The biryani itself was neither great nor terrible, and the tables were passably clean, but the terrible delay and attitude ruined the night.
We stood outside for over 45 minutes despite having a prior reservation, only to be barked at by the floor manager. Once seated, no one even brought menus for another fifteen minutes.
The chef's special railway mutton curry was deeply flavorful with melt-in-mouth cuts. The waitstaff were wonderfully courteous, checking in at just the right times.
Worst service ever experienced. The waiter brought the wrong curry, argued with my husband that we ordered it, and rolled his eyes when we asked for a replacement.

The dum biryani and smoky paneer tikka were heavenly, and the warm Mughal-inspired lighting created a gorgeous, cozy vibe. We paid roughly ₹1,800 which matches the local standard, though the servers were noticeably sluggish and inattentive.
The mutton rogan josh was a pool of oil with hardly any meat, and the naan arrived stone cold and chewy. Really disappointed with the quality of food tonight.
The staff were very kind and apologized repeatedly, but waiting 55 minutes for two plates of biryani is hard to excuse. The tables and plates were decently kept, neither dirty nor sparkling.
The bill came to ₹2,100 for three curries and breads, which is pretty much the prevailing market rate across Koramangala.
Staff was downright dismissive from the moment we walked in. We were practically begging for napkins and drinking water the entire evening.

The mutton dum biryani and garlic naans were absolutely delicious, bursting with authentic flavors. Unfortunately, the staff ignored our table for nearly 20 minutes just to get a refill of water and forgot our extra raita completely.
Hands down the best murgh malai tikka in Bengaluru! Tender, juicy, and charred just right in the tandoor.
Impressed by how spotless everything was. Cutlery was sparkling, floors were thoroughly clean, and the open kitchen area looked genuinely hygienic.
Heavenly dal makhani slow-cooked to creamy perfection, paired with crisp tandoori rotis. You cannot miss their Lucknowi chicken biryani either!
Best paneer tikka ever, super soft and flavorful.
Walked in on a packed Friday evening and had a table within five minutes flat! Our starters arrived astonishingly fast too.
Tried the butter chicken and jeera rice; it was standard fare, neither extraordinarily rich nor bad. Perfectly average North Indian taste.
The warm brass lighting, tasteful Indian instrumental music, and traditional wooden seating make this place feel so regal and relaxing.
Our waiter was very attentive and made sure our toddler had a high chair immediately. Courteous staff throughout.
The hospitality here is unmatched! The captain gave great recommendations and treated us like family from start to finish.
Lovely subtle lighting and comfortable booths that made our dinner date very cozy. The waitstaff was swift and polite whenever we asked for extra chutney.
Stunning interior with elegant jali work that creates a wonderful atmosphere. The seekh kebabs and Awadhi biryani tasted utterly divine.
Their tandoori pomfret is seasoned to absolute perfection! Rich marinades and authentic smoky aroma in every single bite.
Staff handled our large office group with immense patience and split our bill without any fuss.
Generous portions of chicken tikka and biryani for just around ₹450 per head, which is fantastic value. Servers were prompt and smiling the whole evening.
Flavors are phenomenal, especially the bhuna gosht and soft roomali rotis. The tables and floor seemed wiped down normally like any standard restaurant.
Really enjoyed the tandoori mushroom and crisp lachha parathas, seasoned nicely without being overly oily.
Our server Ramesh was exceptional, anticipating everything we needed before we even asked. The decor has the typical North Indian restaurant setup with booth seating, nothing particularly unique.
The staff took great care of us and checked on our table regularly. As for the food, the chicken handi and pudina paratha were top notch!
Phenomenal dining experience! The servers were lightning-quick and courteous, and that signature Saffron Table biryani melted in my mouth.
We waited around fifteen minutes for a table on Sunday afternoon. The food tasted ordinary, similar to most local curry points, and the server did their job without much interaction.
The premises, washrooms, and dining hall were impeccably clean and polished. Sadly, the service was terribly inattentive—we had to wave our hands multiple times just to get the bill.
Huge portion of dum biryani packed with tender meat for only ₹380! Remarkable quality North Indian cuisine that won't burn a hole in your pocket.
Hospitality at its finest. The manager personally ensured our order was customized for my elderly mother's mild spice tolerance.
It was painfully loud and cramped inside, with tables squeezed so close together you can barely move your chair. The harsh glare and noisy setting completely ruined the dining mood.
The floor staff were so warm and attentive throughout our dinner. Our glasses were never empty, and the manager checked in twice to ensure we were enjoying our evening.
Really liked the warm lighting and subtle instrumental music playing in the background. It creates a calm, sophisticated vibe away from the city traffic.
The mutton dum biryani was pure perfection—aromatic rice and incredibly tender meat. On top of that, our waiter was exceptionally prompt and offered fantastic recommendations.
Super fast, courteous service from the moment we walked in. The dining area was cleaned in the usual manner you'd expect at a busy restaurant.
Staff handled our large family gathering really smoothly. Quick with extra plates and very polite whenever we requested refills.
Hands down the best Lucknowi biryani in town! The tandoori chicken had that authentic smoky char, moist right to the bone.
Everything was gleaming clean, from the polished cutlery to the spotless washrooms. Very hygienic standards maintained here.
The servers were very attentive and courteous with our orders. Also really enjoyed the cozy booth seating and tasteful brass decor.
Delicious paneer tikka lababdar paired with piping hot butter naans. The open terrace seating area has a lovely breezy charm in the evening.
Charming vintage North Indian aesthetic with comfortable chairs and soft amber lamps. Great setting for a relaxed dinner date.
Rich, slow-cooked dal makhani that blew us away, along with stellar service from the captain who kept the hot rotis coming in perfect sync.
Incredible tandoori pomfret and succulent galouti kebabs that literally melt in your mouth. Rich, nuanced spices in every single bite!
Our waiter took the order and served the dishes within regular time. Neither overly friendly nor rude, just standard service.
Kudos to the waitstaff for promptly accommodating our request for a milder gravy for our toddler without any fuss.
The murgh malai tikka was seasoned just right and very juicy. The dimly lit, modern heritage dining room makes for a lovely, relaxed evening.
A flawless dining experience! The saffron gosht biryani was divine, the service was genuinely royal, and the palatial interior decor is simply stunning.
Impeccably clean dining room. Tables were thoroughly sanitized before we were seated, and the cutlery arrived sealed and pristine.
The butter chicken was pretty average, tasting like any standard curry house version, but our server was wonderful and extremely polite throughout the meal.
Waited over 45 minutes for a table despite having put our name down, and then another half an hour just for the appetizers to show up. Dreadful waiting experience.
The chicken bhuna and jeera rice were hearty and flavorful, and paying just ₹850 for two people felt like a total bargain for this quality.
Typical restaurant layout without much standout decor, but everything was spotless. Crisp table linens, spotless floor, and clean water glasses.
Really enjoyed the Awadhi biryani. The long grain basmati had absorbed all the saffron and whole spices beautifully.
Loved the rich Mughal-inspired arches and warm lighting. It feels very grand and relaxed, a wonderful escape from the noisy streets outside.
Phenomenal tandoori feast! Portions of seekh kebab and biryani were massive, and our bill was barely ₹1,100 for three of us. Incredible value.
That signature saffron biryani is absolute heaven! Perfectly layered flavors, fragrant ghee aroma, and meat cooked to supreme tenderness.

The wait time was awful, nearly 45 minutes standing by the curb on a Friday night just to get a table. On the bright side, the servers were exceptionally polite and handled the packed house with grace, though the butter chicken and garlic naan tasted fairly average.
Our waiter was attentive without hovering, constantly refilling our water and making sure our courses arrived on time with a warm smile.
The Lucknowi mutton biryani was fragrant, rich, and cooked to absolute perfection. It is just a pity we had to wait almost an hour past our scheduled reservation time just to be seated.

We waited around twenty minutes at the entrance, which was expected for peak hours. However, the staff completely ignored us once we sat down, taking forever to hand over menus and glaring when we asked for sliced onions and lime.
Loved the smoky char on the tandoori pomfret and the dal makhani was simmered to rich perfection. The staff took the order and cleared the plates in a routine, unremarkable manner.
Staff treated my grandparents with incredible warmth and made sure their seats were comfortable. The bill worked out to around ₹1,900 for three of us, which felt about average for this neighborhood.
Stunning heritage decor with warm chandelier lighting and mellow instrumental music playing in the background. The hospitality from the team was top tier from the second we walked in.
Truly phenomenal galouti kebabs that melted like butter, and the kashmiri rogan josh had deep, complex spicing.
The dining floor and tables were spotless, and the handwash area was sparkling clean despite the rush. Sadly, the waitstaff were disorganised and kept forgetting our water and bread orders.
Hands down the most authentic chicken dum biryani in Bengaluru, tender meat and aromatic long-grain rice paired with great burani raita.
Both the stuffed Amritsari kulchas and the paneer lababdar were delicious, and our captain guided us through the specials with genuine enthusiasm.
The Mughal-style arches and warm brass lamps create a gorgeous setting, and every table was wiped down immaculately before guests sat. The reshmi kebabs were incredibly juicy and flavorful.
Made to wait 50 minutes past our booking while the hostess kept telling us 'just five more minutes'.
Waited about fifteen minutes for a table which is typical on a weekend. The Sikandari raan was spectacular, fall-apart tender with bold roasted spices.
The interiors are okay, standard dark wood seating and plain walls, neither memorable nor unpleasant.
Got a table after roughly twenty minutes in line during the lunchtime rush.

The palatial brass arches and tasteful mood lighting give the place a regal feel, and the team treated us like royalty throughout. Still, the curries were just passable, and paying ₹3,400 for what felt like very routine North Indian food definitely pinched the wallet.
Amazing value for money, our feast of mixed tandoori platters and gravies came to barely ₹1,100. Everything tasted fresh and flavourful, and the waitstaff were speedy and polite throughout.
The floor team handled our sudden party of eight effortlessly, managing custom requests with immense patience.
We were stuck waiting outside on the stairs for 45 minutes, but the lovely dim-lit ambiance inside and the outstanding smoked mutton seekh kebabs made up for the frustration.
The servers did their job, took the order, dropped the plates, and brought the bill without any real warmth or issue.
The murgh malai tikka was extraordinarily creamy with just the right hit of crushed cardamom.
Extremely reasonable pricing for such generous portion sizes, total pocket-friendly feast!
Outstanding zafrani paneer and flaky laccha parathas, every single bite was packed with rich, authentic flavor.
Loved the calm, sophisticated interior design with gentle sitar tunes and intimate lighting.
The mutton dum biryani was packed with rich spices and tender meat, and the staff was wonderfully attentive throughout our dinner.
Terrible hospitality. The waiters avoided eye contact for twenty minutes, and when our bill finally arrived, the server practically tossed the folder onto the table without a word.
Our captain was exceptionally polite and made us feel so welcome. He offered fantastic recommendations and anticipated our refills before we even had to ask.
Really loved the warm lighting and tasteful brass decor throughout the dining area. It creates a relaxing, upscale vibe for an evening out.
The paneer tikka and rotis were fairly run-of-the-mill, and the order took the usual twenty minutes to arrive, but charging ₹580 for a tiny bowl of dal is simply unreasonable.
The service was standard. The steward took our order, brought the dishes, and handed over the card machine without much delay or interaction.
The chicken biryani tasted stale and dry, completely devoid of aroma. Paying ₹450 is standard around here, but the preparation was thoroughly disappointing.
Smoky tandoori pomfret with brilliant marinade—thoroughly enjoyed every bite. Food arrived in about 20 minutes, which is quite ordinary for a full restaurant.
Hands down the best galouti kebabs in town. They melt completely on your tongue with that rich saffron aftertaste!
Had the butter chicken and garlic kulcha for lunch. It was acceptable North Indian fare, pretty much identical to any other place nearby.
Outstanding evening! The murgh malai tikka was heavenly, the servers treated us like royalty, and the royal heritage decor makes the space feel truly special.
Charming traditional interiors, very courteous attendants, and the total was barely ₹1100 for two people, which is phenomenal value in this part of Bengaluru.
Their signature Saffron Gosht Biryani is flawless—fragrant long-grain rice, juicy mutton shanks, and perfectly balanced whole spices.
Waited over an hour just to get a table despite reserving in advance, and then sat around another 40 minutes before starters appeared. Ruined our evening completely.
Extremely overpriced menu. They charged ₹180 for two plain tandoori rotis and ₹420 for basic raita; complete rip off.
Crisp rumali rotis paired with slow-cooked bhuna gosht—hearty, authentic comfort food done right.
A painful 55-minute delay just for two portions of chicken biryani on a quiet Tuesday afternoon. Horrible kitchen pacing.
The cozy booth seating and lovely instrumental music made for a great setting, and the waiter did his job okay, but the fish tikka was rubbery and lacked any seasoning.
Rich rogan josh and buttery naans tasted superb, but the dining hall was deafeningly noisy and the tables were crammed so close together that people kept bumping into my chair.
The tandoor items are packed with smoky goodness and bursting with flavor, but waiting nearly an hour at the table for food to arrive test our patience.
The prices are remarkably wallet-friendly with full curries under ₹350, though standing in the lobby for 45 minutes before getting seated was exhausting.
Platters came out in about fifteen to twenty minutes, which is pretty standard for a dinner rush.
Rich dal makhani simmered to perfection and the tandoori chicken had that authentic char. Absolutely delicious North Indian fare!
We were seated immediately on a busy weekend and our hot kebabs reached the table in under ten minutes flat.
Loved the warm amber lighting, subtle saffron motifs on the walls, and comfortable lounge seating.
The dining area and washrooms were kept in an ordinary state, just standard cleanliness like any typical city restaurant.
Way too expensive for basic North Indian fare. Charging 480 rupees for a small handi of paneer butter masala is pure daylight robbery.
Best Lucknowi mutton biryani in town! Meat was fall-apart tender and the fragrant long-grain rice had the exact right touch of kewra.
Had a blast here on Friday night. The tandoori pomfret and garlic naan were heavenly, and our waiter made sure our water glasses and plates were swapped promptly.

The floor staff were so warm and attentive throughout our dinner, guiding us through spice levels. The prices are pretty average for a sit-down place here, around 400 rupees a curry.
Pathetic attitude from the waitstaff. The server practically threw the bill booklet on our table and vanished when we asked for an extra plate.
Waited over an hour and ten minutes just for a table for two, only to watch them seat walk-ins ahead of us. Complete disaster management on weekends.
The dal makhani and rotis were decent enough, standard taste. But what won me over was how affordable it was—hardly 700 rupees for two—and the captain was so courteous and attentive.
We waited about 15 minutes to be seated on a Wednesday night.
Outstanding Murgh Malai Tikka! Melts right in the mouth, perfectly charred without being dry. The team serving us was super cheerful and quick to bring hot naans straight from the tandoor.
Our table took about twenty minutes to free up, which is pretty normal for peak dinner hour. The chicken dum biryani and burani raita were top tier though, worth every bite!
Got seated in about ten minutes, so the delay was normal. But the pricing is absurd—charging 550 rupees for four tiny pieces of seekh kebab is just not worth it.
Sensational butter chicken, rich without feeling greasy, paired with crispy lachha parathas. Price point is what you would expect in this part of Bengaluru, around 1500 rupees for a couple.
Loved the warm, dimly lit interiors with subtle instrumental tracks playing in the background. The galouti kebabs were deeply flavorful and fragrant.
Horrible food. The mutton biryani smelled stale and the chicken tikka was dry as cardboard and burnt black on the skewers.
The kakori kebabs and rogan josh were genuinely delicious and rich in flavor. Unfortunately, the waiters completely ignored us half the night and took 25 minutes just to fetch a bottle of water.
That smoky aroma on their tandoori chicken is absolute perfection. Truly authentic Punjabi flavors, easily my favorite spot in Bangalore.
Really cozy vibe inside with tasteful brass accents and traditional jali woodwork. Creates such an inviting and relaxed atmosphere for an evening out.
Everything from the tables to the polished cutlery was spotless and squeaky clean. Food was divine—the dahi ke kebab and bhuna gosht were bursting with fresh spices.
Unbelievably good zafrani biryani! Each grain of basmati was coated in fragrant spices and the chicken was ultra juicy.
The tawa chaap and butter naan hit the spot nicely. Wait time was about 15-20 mins before ordering, which seemed typical for dinner.
Stood outside sweating for 50 minutes even though we were told it would take ten minutes. The crowd management at the door is terrible.
A 15 minute wait at the door was totally fine given the rush. Once seated, the staff took wonderful care of us, and the mutton nihari with khamiri roti was sheer perfection.
The brass lanterns and warm wooden decor give Saffron Table such a rich, elegant vibe. Service was typical, no complaints or anything remarkable, but the environment makes it a lovely dining spot.
The staff here is genuinely phenomenal. Our server was so attentive, constantly checking if we needed more warm rumali rotis, and handled our large family gathering with utmost grace.
Such hospitable management! They immediately swapped out our dish when we asked for less spice without an ounce of hesitation.
The mutton seekh kebab melted right in the mouth, but ₹680 for just four small pieces feels like daylight robbery. Delicious cooking, but your wallet will hurt.
Really disappointed with the chicken dum biryani. Rice was bone dry, the chicken pieces were tough and rubbery, and the salan had a weird sour aftertaste.

Had to endure a painful 45-minute wait out on the pavement before getting a table, which was exhausting. However, once inside, the dim lighting and classical ghazal music create an exquisite vibe, and the hospitality from the captains was stellar throughout.

The saffron special gosht biryani was packed with rich flavor, and the floor staff attended to us promptly and politely. We queued for about 20 minutes on a Friday night, and the decor and tables were standard for a central Bengaluru diner, reasonably neat. It definitely tilts on the expensive side with bills crossing ₹2500 for two, but the culinary quality and gracious service won me over.
We had to wait almost 40 mins for a table on Saturday night, which tested our patience. Thankfully, the servers were extremely polite, and the paneer tikka lababdar with butter naan tasted heavenly.
The staff went above and beyond to make us comfortable and even offered extra mint chutney with a smile. Sadly, the dal makhani was overly salty and the tandoori roti was burnt crisp on the edges.
Sat down after the expected 15-minute wait time. The Lucknowi biryani here is simply unbeatable in Bangalore, fragrant rice and succulent meat cooked to absolute perfection!
Top-notch dining experience! The murgh malai kebab was bursting with smoky flavor, our attendant gave great recommendations, and paying under ₹1200 for such a feast was an absolute bargain.

The interior decor is breathtaking, with intricate brass lanterns and royal Mughal accents everywhere you look. Had the standard veg thali which was fairly average north indian fare, but the gorgeous setting made for a memorable evening.
Hands down the best tandoori pomfret in town! Rich marination, perfect char, and juicy throughout.
The butter chicken and garlic kulcha were decent, nothing exceptional to write home about. The dining area was passably tidy, though a couple of stray crumbs were still on the chair when we sat.
The decor is just a standard restaurant setup with generic modern seating and background music you barely notice.
Their tandoori chicken is smoky and tender, easily some of the best North Indian cooking around. But waiting over an hour just to get a basic two-seater on a weekday is ridiculous.
Loved the velvety texture of the subz handi and garlic naans. But ₹520 for a small bowl of vegetables is just way overpriced.
Got seated in about ten minutes, as estimated by the host. Spotless cutlery, sparkling clean glasses, and gleaming marble tables—hygiene is clearly taken very seriously here.
Regular mixed veg platter and jeera rice, tastes like standard home cooking with nothing unique. That said, ₹650 total for a hearty lunch in this location is surprisingly affordable.
Was pleasantly shocked by the final bill—getting this full on gourmet North Indian food for just ₹400 per person in central Bangalore is a steal!
Waiting 50 minutes on an empty stomach was definitely annoying. Still, the waiters treated us like kings once we got inside, and the raan biryani was sensational enough to justify everything.
Walked in during Sunday lunch rush and got escorted straight to a booth without waiting a single minute!
Loved the romantic candlelit atmosphere and soft sitar music playing in the background. The stewards were impeccably mannered, pulling out chairs and refreshing drinks seamlessly.

Stood at the door for 45 minutes despite a prior reservation, and the hostess barely acknowledged us. When we finally sat down, waiters completely ignored our table and took 20 minutes just to bring water.
The tandoori platter here is pure bliss, especially the dahi ke kebab which just melt on your tongue.
Menu prices are typical for dining out in this area, around ₹400 to ₹500 for a main course.

The Lucknowi dum biryani and tandoori chicken tasted genuinely fantastic, but the experience was ruined by indifferent staff who kept ignoring us. We waited around 20 minutes for our table, which is typical for a Saturday night, and the bill came to around ₹1400 for two. However, the dining hall was deafeningly loud and stuffy with practically no AC cooling.
Our server was so attentive and polite throughout dinner! Really appreciated how warmly they handled our family.
Gorgeous warm lighting and beautiful brass decor that sets a lovely mood for an evening out. The team was exceptionally welcoming and ensured our water glasses were never empty.
The butter chicken and garlic naan are rich, smoky, and absolutely delicious. But waiting nearly an hour just to get seated on a weekday evening is simply ridiculous.
Standard restaurant setup with typical North Indian decor and background instrumental music playing.

Beautiful interior aesthetic with comfortable booths and subtle warm lighting. The mutton seekh kebabs and dal makhani were cooked to perfection! The 15-minute wait for a table was expected, though our waiter seemed terribly distracted and forgot our lime soda order entirely.
The atmosphere here is stunning, especially the rooftop seating area with pleasant Bangalore evening breeze. Had the chicken tikka roll and lassi, both were standard restaurant fare.
Charging ₹480 for a basic paneer butter masala and ₹95 for a single tandoori roti is pure daylight robbery. My wallet took a massive hit for a very ordinary meal.
We stood outside for over 45 minutes despite having put our names down early. The interior has ordinary tables and simple decor, nothing special enough to justify that endless queue.
It felt like sitting in a crowded railway station concourse rather than a restaurant. The seating is crammed so tight that waiters kept bumping into my chair every two minutes.
Hands down some of the best murgh malai kebabs in Bangalore! Melting in the mouth, perfectly marinated, and full of smoky tandoor flavor.
Really good food overall, especially their signature Awadhi biryani which had fragrant long-grain basmati and tender meat. Would definitely order again.
Was seated within barely two minutes of stepping in on a Friday night, and our starters showed up in less than ten minutes.

Had to wait almost 40 minutes for our table, but the rest of the evening made up for it completely. The charming vintage decor and soft ghazals created such a refined vibe, and our captain was so gracious and apologetic about the delay.
Ordered the veg pulao and yellow dal tadka, which tasted fine and neither impressed nor disappointed. The interiors look like any standard family dining place in the city.
Walked right in and got a corner table immediately with zero delay, and the food arrived promptly. Had the egg biryani which tasted quite average, but the speed of everything was unbeatable.
Staff was very courteous and replaced a wrong dish without any fuss. The total was around ₹800 which is normal, but the paneer tikka was rubbery and lacked any real spice or smoke.
The waitstaff were super polite and served us with genuine smiles. But paying ₹650 plus taxes for a small handi of chicken curry feels way overpriced.
Terrible experience with the food. The mutton biryani was dry, the meat smelled stale, and the raita was sour and spoiled.
The stuffed kulchas and dal bukhara here are sheer perfection. Authentic North Indian flavors that hit the spot every single time!

Got seated instantly without any queue. The food was outstanding, especially the smoky bhuna gosht and crisp roomali rotis, while the waiter just did his basic job taking orders and bringing the bill.
We waited about 15 minutes for a table, which is quite standard for dinner time around here. The kashmiri pulao and tandoori prawns were phenomenal, packed with aromatic spices and so fresh.
Outstanding dining experience! The staff treated us like royalty, recommending great combinations, and the chicken reshmi kebab alongside the butter naan tasted absolutely divine.

The food itself was actually very flavorful—the tandoori platter was seasoned nicely. But they charge nearly ₹2500 for two people to sit in a dark, noisy, cramped room with glaring fluorescent lights by the kitchen door.
The staff just took our order, delivered the plates, and brought the bill when asked.
